newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Passenger ship with 290 aboard adrift in Pacific.
newsitem.headline: Passenger ship with 290 aboard adrift in Pacific.

text.p: A charter ship with 290 passengers is adrift in the central Pacific without power after a fire in the engine room, Australian maritime officials said on Wednesday.

The 64.5-metre long Maasmond was en-route from Tarawa Island in the Kiribati Islands to Christmas Island when a fire in its engine room disabled the ship late on Tuesday and forced it to ask for assistance, Australian Maritime Safety Authority spokesman David Gray told Reuters.

Gray said a Royal New Zealand Air Force search plane and a Royal New Zealand Navy patrol boat had been dispatched to help the boat, which was drifting about 800 kms east of Tarawa in the Kiribati Islands, a group of coral atolls about 5,000 kms north-east of Sydney.
Gray said it was not clear from the distress message if the fire was out, but that the ship had requested a tow.
New Zealand Air Force officials were not immediately available for comment on the distressed ship.
The ship was registered in Kingston, Jamaica, Gray added.
